Stilly.desc: Constantly consolidates and repairs the roster in-season. Best when turning several good assets into one elite one, or escaping a draft mistake before the market fully collapses.
Stilly.best: 2023 Cooper Kupp → Mike Evans + Derrick Henry; 2024 CMC escape + Chase Brown
Stilly.scar: 2020 Shitter Bowl champion; Mitch owns the verified Sleeper series 9–1.
Stilly.draft: Jayden Daniels at 14.140 in 2024; later became a 2026 keeper.

JMid.desc: Frequently one major deal away from fixing the roster—and the deal can create two new problems. Immediately showed elite scoring upside in the first full season in the current group.
JMid.best: 2024 James Cook → Kyren Williams + Calvin Ridley
JMid.scar: 2025: 5–9 with the lowest broad lineup-efficiency mark in the league.
JMid.draft: 2024 Ladd McConkey at 9.87 and Chuba Hubbard at 12.114 stand out.

Tom.desc: Old-school roster builder who can lose isolated trade grades and still assemble a team that wins when it matters. The league’s benchmark because four titles are the only argument that really ends arguments.
Tom.best: 2022 CeeDee + DK + DeVonta package; 2024 Andrews + Dowdle helped stabilize title run
Tom.scar: Regular-season résumé is less dominant than the trophy case suggests.
Tom.draft: 2020 Josh Allen in Round 8; 2022 Garrett Wilson in Round 11; 2024 Chase Brown in Round 10.

Stew.peak: 2022 · 11–3 · best record, PF and potential PF
Stew.desc: The league’s highest-volume transaction personality. At his best, he manufactures elite rosters; at his worst, the extra move after the good move is the one that ends up in the museum.
Stew.best: 2022 Justin Jefferson and Ja’Marr Chase acquisitions; Puka Nacua for $6 in 2023
Stew.scar: 2023 Jefferson + Josh Jacobs → Gabe Davis after the future first was voided.
Stew.draft: 2022 Kenneth Walker at 10.94; 2024 J.K. Dobbins at 13.124.

Scott.desc: Smallest career sample among the current group, but already owns a title. The 2025 championship paired strong lineup efficiency with a postseason hammer.
Scott.scar: 2026 Week 2: 46.38, the lowest known Sleeper-era score.
Scott.draft: 2024 Rashee Rice at 7.69; 2026 Bijan kept as a Round 1 foundation.

Mitch.desc: Builds teams that look like solvable equations: elite anchors, efficient lineup construction, and relentlessly high regular-season output. The missing championship is the only obvious hole.
Mitch.best: 2022 Saquon + Thielen for Jonathan Taylor; sustained elite regular-season construction
Mitch.scar: 2025 semifinal: MHJ 1.9 over Chris Rodriguez 13.4; exact lineup flip would have advanced him.
Mitch.draft: 2020 Antonio Gibson at 11.103; 2024 JSN in Round 9 became a 2025/26 core asset.

Tony.desc: Often less noisy than Stew, but historically excellent at turning trades and waivers into usable points. Has one of the league’s strongest title-season transaction résumés.
Tony.best: 2021 Joe Mixon for James Robinson + Zack Moss; 2022 Kenneth Walker for $94 FAAB
Tony.scar: 2025 playoff loss by 0.72 with Tony Pollard’s 17.7 on the bench over Kenneth Walker’s 2.4.
Tony.draft: 2020 Stefon Diggs at 7.61; 2023 Raheem Mostert at 14.131.

Stover.desc: Often owns a roster that looks worth more than the weekly score. Strong overall résumé: a title, 50 Sleeper wins, and another season with the league’s best record.
Stover.scar: 2024 Malik Nabers-for-Davante outcome and the expensive Jauan Jennings claim.
Stover.draft: 2024 Brian Thomas Jr. at 10.91 was one of the best value picks of that draft.

Kuhl.desc: Repeatedly makes useful acquisitions but has one of the league’s weakest conversion records. The archive contains both sharp moves and catastrophic realized-value losses.
Kuhl.best: 2023 Kyren Williams for $21; 2024 J.K. Dobbins acquisition
Kuhl.scar: 2023 Ja’Marr Chase → Tyler Lockett after future picks were voided; repeated lineup-conversion misses.
Kuhl.draft: 2023 Rashee Rice at 15.144; 2024 Xavier Worthy at 8.78.

Birch.desc: Will hit on 17, draw a four, and then explain why it was the correct play. The résumé has real wins behind the chaos: a title, 50 Sleeper wins, and several strong positional trades.
Birch.best: 2021 Lamar + Mark Andrews + Josh Jacobs positional-advantage trade
Birch.scar: 2022 Ja’Marr Chase → Patterson + Jeff Wilson + Claypool.
Birch.draft: 2021 James Conner at 11.105; 2022 Brandon Aiyuk at 10.91.

trades.title: Stilly acquires Mike Evans + Derrick Henry
trades.why: Direct championship-building move. From Weeks 9–17, Evans + Henry produced about 257.5 half-PPR points versus about 84.8 for Kupp: roughly +172.7 raw ROS points before lineup context.
trades.counter: This is the cleanest example of a trade that wins both the process and outcome tests.

trades.title: Stew sends Justin Jefferson + Josh Jacobs
trades.why: The future first was the only way to defend the package. Once the league voided future-pick trading, the realized historical return became Jefferson + Jacobs for Gabe Davis.
trades.counter: The site does not invent a full alternate record, because that would require guessing Stew’s weekly lineup and downstream transactions.

trades.title: Birch sends Ja’Marr Chase
trades.got: Cordarrelle Patterson + Jeff Wilson + Chase Claypool
trades.why: One of the strongest all-time value-loss candidates. Chase remained an elite difference-maker; the return did not create comparable positional or weekly value.
trades.counter: A pure realized-value loss, even before considering how hard elite WR production is to replace.

trades.title: Tony acquires Joe Mixon
trades.why: The cleanest pure-value win of Tony’s championship season. It consolidated replaceable depth into a premium RB during the title run.
trades.counter: This is exactly the type of deal the Trade Lab rewards: concentration into a more valuable weekly starter.

trades.title: Stilly escapes Christian McCaffrey
trades.sent: Christian McCaffrey + Diontae Johnson + Tee Higgins
trades.got: Terry McLaurin + De’Von Achane + Tank Dell
trades.why: The 1.01 CMC disaster could have sunk the season. The trade converted one unavailable cornerstone plus secondary assets into multiple usable starters and helped fuel a runner-up finish.
trades.counter: The Hall treats this as roster repair, not simply player-for-player surplus.

trades.title: Stilly’s Ja’Marr Chase asset chain
trades.sent: Jahmyr Gibbs + RJ Harvey (W3), then Ja’Marr Chase in W11
trades.got: Ja’Marr Chase + Chase Brown, then Amon-Ra + Jordan Addison + Jared Goff
trades.why: This is a multi-stage keeper-era trade tree, not a single transaction. Amon-Ra became a 2026 Round 1 keeper and the chain still has future value.
trades.counter: The right grade changes as downstream assets keep producing.
